wiktionary.gloss: A period between set dates that mark a year, such as from January 1 to December 31 by the Gregorian calendar, from Tishri 1 to Elul 29 by the Jewish calendar, and from Muharram 1 to Dhu al-Hijjah 29 or 30 by the Islamic calendar.

examples: During this school year I have to get up at 6:30 to catch the bus.
wiktionary.gloss: A scheduled part of a calendar year spent in a specific activity.

examples: Every second-year student must select an area of specialization.
The exams in year 12 at high school are the most difficult.
wiktionary.gloss: A level or grade in school or college.

examples: Geneticists have created baker's yeast that can live to 800 in yeast years.
wiktionary.gloss: The proportion of a creature's lifespan equivalent to one year of an average human lifespan (see also dog year).

idioms.gloss: A wish said around the start of a new year to wish someone well for the New Year (holiday) or for the (entire) new year.
The current year. (This entry is a translation hub.)
Used to emphasize the annual distinctiveness of Christmas, especially in contexts where either the special joys or tribulations of the holiday are described.
